newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks surge to record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks surge to record high at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks surged to a new life-time high at the open on Wednesday, defying New York's drop. * Banks, utilities, consumer products and golds all up more than one percent.
Toronto stocks surged to new highs at the open on Wednesday as banks, consumer products, golds and utilities all climbed more than one percent.
Traders said most gains were made by interest-sensitive stocks after U.S. consumer prices came in lower than expected this morning in the day and allayed fears of a rate rise.
"Most of it's on the back of the banks...utilities are (also) all very interest-sensitive, they have huge debts so any time rates come down they have huge savings," one said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index jumped 49.91 points to a new high of 6705.84 at the open.
Total trading volume was 7.7 million shares worth C$120.4 million. Advancing stocks outpaced declines 252 to 174, while 215 issues traded flat.
All but two of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes climbed.
Banks gained 76.17 points or 1.06 percent to 7285.68 while utilities surged 1.19 percent to 5685.40.
Real estate and merchandising traded just below even.
U.S. consumer prices came in weaker than expected this morning, rising 0.1 percent in June from April. Economists had forecast a rise of 0.2 percent.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bank shares climbed in early trade, led by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce which rose 0.90 to 37.55 in heavy trade. Toronto-Dominion Bank was up 0.80 to 43.10 while Bank of Montreal climbed 1.00 to 57.40.
